sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Pendleton County
sections.html:
Every land record in the county ends up in Falmouth, at the Pendleton County Clerk's office, 233 Main Street, Room 1 (KY 41040). Letters go to PO Box 112, calls to 859-654-3380 and faxes to 859-654-5600.

Weekday service runs from half past eight until four. On two Saturdays a month, the second and the last, the office stays open until noon, except on holiday weekends. Recording happens where the land is (KRS 142.050 points to KRS 382.110 on this), so a house near Butler or DeMossville is recorded in Falmouth even when the seller has moved away.

Pendleton County is a rural county of rolling hills about midway between Cincinnati and Lexington, inside the Cincinnati metro area. Falmouth is the seat and Butler is the other city. Population sat at 14,644 in 2020 and is estimated at 14,800 for mid-2025.

  • Owner-occupied homes are worth $159,800 at the median, and 74.7 percent of households own.
  • A mortgage holder pays $1,172 monthly, and a renter pays $793.
  • The median household earns $64,669.
  • Commutes average 36.4 minutes.
  • No building permits were recorded for 2025, so nearly every sale is an existing house.

Of the 6,263 housing units counted in 2020, 11.7 percent were vacant, so empty or seasonal property is part of the picture.

Flat charges by document type are set out on the clerk's Document Fees page, which cites KRS 64.012. State transfer tax is extra.

Pendleton County Clerk recording fees
DocumentFee
Mortgage$80
Mortgage with assignment$126

Deed exempt from the state fee$46
Deed that includes a release$96
Judgment lien$46

Affidavit of descent$50

Copies run $5 certified and $2 plain. A package that mixes document types adds up quickly, so ask for a single quoted total first.

sections.h2: What has to appear in a deed before the clerk files it?
sections.html:
KRS 382.135 forbids a clerk to file a deed missing any of these four things.

  • Each party's full name and mailing address.
  • The entire price, written as consideration.
  • A care-of address for the tax bill that covers the transfer year.
  • A sworn, notarized statement from both parties that the price shown is the whole price, or for a gift an estimate of fair cash value.

Deeds limited to utility easements, government rights of way or cemetery lots, and deeds fixing mistakes in an earlier deed, are excused from the last three items.

sections.h2: How transfer tax works on a sale
sections.html:
The grantor pays fifty cents on every $500 of value, counting a partial $500 as whole, before the deed is accepted (KRS 142.050). The clerk retains 5 percent as a collection fee, and the county treasurer receives the rest quarterly.

Corrective deeds, deeds that give or lift security for a debt, spouse transfers, foreclosure transfers and parent-to-child transfers for token money escape the tax. A gift is measured by what the house would sell for on the open market.

When a house comes down through a will or intestacy, the personal representative must file an affidavit with the clerk before the estate closes, naming each recipient and what the property is worth (KRS 382.135(4)). The clerk lists $50 for an affidavit of descent and $46 for a will.

Liens go on record at the same counter. Recording a certificate of delinquency costs $46, and so does its release. Unpaid property tax passes from the sheriff to the County Clerk after April 15, and a lien is recorded on the parcel. Judgment and mechanics' liens cost $46 in each direction. A parcel search at the clerk's counter before listing can head off surprises.

• Find the deed book and page for your own title.
  • See whether a lien, lis pendens or certificate of delinquency is on record.
  • Pick the mailing address for the buyer's first bill.
  • Book a notary for the sworn price statement.
  • Request one total for recording fees and transfer tax.

Why each step matters: the deed book and page let the title agent find your chain of ownership quickly. The search for a lien, lis pendens or certificate shows whether a lawsuit or old tax debt is attached. The mailing address keeps the buyer's first bill from landing in the wrong mailbox, and the notary has to witness the sworn statement before the clerk will accept the deed. One quoted total for fees and tax lets you budget for closing without a surprise at the counter.

An heir with an empty Pendleton County house who would rather not make repairs can ask for a cash offer, and the buyer's closing agent then takes care of recording.

Call 859-654-3380 and ask for one total on everything you plan to file, including the transfer tax, since fees vary by document type and a package that mixes types adds up. Bring the signed and notarized deed and the sworn statement of price. Know the mailing address where the buyer wants the first tax bill sent, because the clerk cannot file the deed without it.

If a lien or certificate turns up in a search, ask for a written payoff and the $46 release fee at the same visit, so the title is clean when the deed goes on record. Weekday hours are the surest bet. The second and last Saturday mornings are available too, but not on holiday weekends.

sections.h2: Other documents that come up in a sale
sections.html:
A few filings beyond the deed show up in sales and estates. A power of attorney costs $50 to record, which matters when someone signs for an owner who cannot be at closing. A plat is $50. A mortgage runs $80, and one that includes an assignment runs $126. A deed that carries a release inside it is $96, against $50 for a plain deed, so combining documents can change the bill.

Judgment liens, releases and a certificate of delinquency are each $46. Each old filing therefore carries its own recording cost, on top of whatever debt sits behind it. Ask the clerk for the full list of what is recorded against the parcel before you set a closing date.

For an estate, the personal representative files an affidavit listing each heir and the value of the property before the estate closes. The affidavit of descent costs $50, and recording a will costs $46. Heirs who live out of town should line up a notary and decide on one mailing address for the first tax bill before the deed is signed.

faqs.q: What hours does the Pendleton County Clerk keep?
faqs.a: Weekdays from 8:30 a.m. until 4 p.m., and on the second and last Saturday of each month until noon, barring a holiday weekend.

faqs.q: What does recording a Pendleton County deed cost?
faqs.a: The clerk lists $50 for a plain deed, $96 when a release is included and $46 when the deed is exempt from the state fee.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on a Pendleton County sale?
faqs.a: The seller, as grantor, at fifty cents per $500 of value with a partial $500 counted whole. The clerk collects it before accepting the deed.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a lien release in Pendleton County?
faqs.a: $46 for a release of a lien or mortgage, and the same for recording a certificate of delinquency.

faqs.q: Where can I get a certified copy of my deed?
faqs.a: At the Pendleton County Clerk in Falmouth, which charges $5 for a certified copy and $2 for a standard one.
